findings.evidence: jobs-probe.mjs creates an independent Docker lifecycle without acquiring the canonical /run/orloom-verifier-lock/slot.lock flock. Its launcher-state file is private to this draft, so it cannot serialize with or reconcile the production verifier slot.

The draft clones and checks out a candidate Git bundle, then tars the checkout including .git. It verifies rows in a separate source SHA list, but does not use the reviewed raw-blob extractCandidateBundle manifest path, the image's run-check.js per-file rehash, or suite-policy admitSuiteInput. Its entry checks only package and lock hashes, so the claimed equivalent admission is false.

The guest entry does not symlink the image-baked /opt/orloom-verifier/node_modules or prepare/freeze /work/source as run-repo-suite.js does. The candidate transfer's precompiled payload is not the trusted clean build path used by this draft.

Host tar and docker-start children are not both awaited with error and close/status checks; exit only is watched for docker-start. A tar failure, spawn error, or stream failure can leave an ambiguous run classified from incomplete output.

The state record is written as creating before Docker create. If create returns an error after an ambiguous side effect, cid remains empty and finally removes the state record. The exact container may remain with its recovery identity lost. A missing final cgroup sample or failed event retrieval also lacks a fail-closed evidence classification.

The TAP success regex expects '# pass 1' after each named subtest, but the recorded parent test summary reports 3 tests and 3 passes. Output text matching is not bound to complete TAP structure or unique named outcomes.

The helper requires a candidate-890 image label, yet the retained executed suite image is labeled for 4d1. The draft has no reviewed image build and stage path for the new image; the transfer lacks probe-bindings.json at the expected incoming path. Static node --check evidence does not establish executable readiness.
